name: Tokyo vege ramen veJin（ベジン） (Tokyo Vege Ramen veJin)

claims.text: The shop's entire menu is 100%-plant-based — no meat, fish, eggs, or dairy are used in any dish or broth on site, which removes animal-product cross-contact for vegan diners (though wheat allergens are not addressed).
Broths, chashu (soy meat), and toppings are all formulated to be free of meat, fish, egg, and dairy as the shop's core concept, rather than as a special off-menu accommodation.

name: 鶏そば かぐら屋 西新宿店 (Torisoba Kaguraya Nishi-Shinjuku)

claims.text: Shoyu-style and tsukemen tare are built on soy sauce combined with katsuobushi, saba-bushi, niboshi and konbu dashi; standard Japanese soy sauce is wheat-based and no gluten-free alternative was mentioned in any source.

name: 月島もんじゃ おこげ 浅草 (Tsukishima Monjya Okoge Asakusa)

claims.text: Skilled staff grill the monjayaki tableside for guests, which some reviewers note makes it approachable for first-timers, though this addresses cooking skill rather than allergen safety.

The shop's signature mame-kanten is made from a short, identifiable ingredient list — Hokkaido red peas simmered about five hours, kanten agar, and kuromitsu syrup — with no meat, fish, or dashi in the base recipe.

The shop's tare (grilling sauce) is a soy-sauce-based sauce that has been continuously topped up since the restaurant opened in 1861, giving the eel its dark, slightly sweet glaze — this traditional style of tare is soy-sauce-based and therefore contains wheat.

The house dashi used in the okonomiyaki/monjayaki batter is made from katsuobushi (bonito flakes), an animal product, and is described as a specialty of the kitchen, with no plant-based dashi alternative found.

name: うさぎ（神泉のらぁめん屋 うさぎ） (Usagi)

claims.text: The signature ramen is built on a traditional shoyu (soy sauce) broth; standard Japanese soy sauce is brewed from both wheat and soybeans, so the broth is not gluten-free.

name: ヴィーガン スシ トウキョウ (Vegan Sushi Tokyo)

claims.text: The entire kitchen and menu are vegan — no fish, meat, egg, or dairy is used anywhere on the menu, so there is no risk of cross-contact with animal products for vegan diners.
Described by reviewers as Japan's first specialized vegan sushi restaurant, built specifically so vegan visitors don't have to compromise on traditional sushi experiences.
